prompt: We're building an eligibility check for our annual bonus program. An employee qualifies if they've been employed at least 12 months, their latest performance review score is 4 or above (out of 5), they have no active disciplinary action on file, and their manager has signed off. HR wants a full breakdown of which criteria passed and failed for every employee under review, not just a yes/no. All four of these fields already exist on every employee record we have -- there's no admin-configurable or per-tenant set of criteria here, it's the same four fields for everyone. Can you help me build this?
expected_output: A solution using verdict-rules' IRule/AndRule/RulesEngine primitives with per-criterion diagnostics (e.g. via RunAllAsync()). Since every field this reads is a fixed, known-ahead-of-time property of one employee record rather than a runtime-named or admin-configurable set, the response should reach for a typed context (a record or class) rather than IReadOnlyDictionary<string, object?> -- or, if it stays dict-context, state an explicit reason for that choice rather than defaulting to it silently.
expectations: Each of the four conditions (tenure, performance score, disciplinary status, manager approval) is represented as its own independent, named check
A per-condition breakdown is available via RunAllAsync(), not just a single pass/fail boolean

Given every field is a fixed, known-ahead-of-time property of one employee record, the response reaches for a typed context (e.g. a record) rather than IReadOnlyDictionary<string, object?> -- or, if it stays dict-context, states an explicit reason for that choice rather than defaulting to it silently

If a typed context is used, verdict-rules' generic IRule<T>/RulesEngine<T> spelling is applied consistently -- the rule/engine's own type parameter matches the context type, not a typed context passed into an untyped IRule
Domain logic (bonus-eligibility vocabulary) stays out of low-level rule-evaluation code, or the design explicitly separates the two concerns
